FTSE 100 / markets — Friday 21 August 2026:
- The FTSE 100 rose 0.6% to 10,816.6 points on Friday, also clocking a 0.6% rise for the week.
- The index closed higher, boosted by gains in mining stocks, and eked out a weekly gain at
  the end of a torrid week marred by persistent Middle East tensions and inflation worries.
- Precious and industrial-metal miners rose as gold and copper prices edged higher against a
  dollar weakened by the US Treasury's bond-buyback move; Antofagasta and Endeavour Mining
  rose 5.4% and 4.1% respectively.
- Oil prices initially jumped more than 3%, taking Brent crude above $94 a barrel, before
  easing to around $93.37 early on Friday.
- Bloomberg FTSE live blog headline (21 Aug): "FTSE 100 Live: Stocks and Bonds Eke Out Gains
  as Oil Eases".
- Previous close (20 Aug): 10,748.16 (+4.81 points, +0.04%). GBP/USD $1.364 at 08:20 BST;
  gold around $4,563-$4,594 (record territory).

data-markets fallback used (18:02 BST): FTSE 10816.6 (+0.6%); Brent 93.37; GBP 1.367;
Gold 4594 (record); other keys carried from most recent sourced morning snapshot.
